title: Buckaroo Bowl I
dek: Buckaroo Bowl I was the first championship game of the Buckaroo Football League, a two-week total over NFL weeks 17 and 18 of 2023 in which Habibsters (Kaushal) erased a 19.8-point deficit to beat Team Pillbert (Alan) 251.36-192.08 and claim the league's first title.
body: Buckaroo Bowl I concluded the inaugural season of the Buckaroo Football League, a six-team league on ESPN founded in 2023. As the first championship in league history, it had no prior champion to defend it, and neither finalist entered with an earlier title. The game was scored as a two-week total across NFL weeks 17 and 18.

Habibsters, managed by Kaushal, entered as the No. 1 seed after a 10-4 regular season in which the team scored 1,528.8 points, the higher total of the two finalists. Team Pillbert, managed by Alan, was the No. 2 seed at 9-5 with 1,499.3 points, just 29.5 behind over the full regular season. Luffy rated the matchup close to a coin flip, giving Habibsters a 52% chance at the title and Team Pillbert 48%.

The two teams split their regular-season meetings. Team Pillbert won the first in week 5 by a lopsided 116.72-75.76, while Habibsters took the rematch in week 10 by a narrow 109.48-106.44. With one blowout each way and almost nothing separating them in seeding or points, the final was billed as the tiebreaker the regular season never provided.

Both finalists reached the Buckaroo Bowl through two-week semifinals played over NFL weeks 15 and 16. Habibsters beat Dawgs (Mekhi) 237.54-196.12, a 41.42-point margin. Christian McCaffrey carried that semifinal for Habib with 61.3 points, the top individual total for either finalist in the round.

Team Pillbert advanced past The fumblers (Randy) 234.86-216.44, an 18.42-point margin in the tighter of the two semifinals. Jalen Hurts led Philly's side with 45.4 points. Each team therefore arrived in the final behind a single star who had just posted a big two-week number, and both of those stars would score far less in the championship.

No in-game play-by-play exists for Buckaroo Bowl I, as the league website did not begin recording in-game events until week 7 of 2026. The account below is drawn from weekly and player totals only, and does not describe the order of scoring within either week.

In NFL week 17, Team Pillbert built a 131.4-111.6 lead, a cushion of 19.8 points. Kyren Williams led Alan's lineup with 29.1 points, supported by Jalen Hurts (19.2), Joe Mixon (16.7), Deebo Samuel (15.7), David Njoku (14.4), Tyreek Hill (10.6) and Cooper Kupp (10.7). For Habibsters, Josh Allen posted 21.2 points, Dak Prescott 20.3, Amon-Ra St. Brown 19.1 and the Bills D/ST 19, while the running backs struggled: Tony Pollard scored 5.4, Rachaad White 6.6 and Austin Ekeler 3.5.

Week 18 reversed the game. Habibsters scored 139.8 points while Team Pillbert managed 60.7, a weekly gap of 79.1 points that turned a 19.8-point deficit into a 59.3-point victory. Prescott (25.2), St. Brown (23.9), Allen (23.1), Calvin Ridley (19.6), Evan Engram (18.9) and the Jets D/ST (18) all contributed for Kaushal's side.

Team Pillbert's week 18 output came almost entirely from Mixon (24.2) and Hill (17.7). Hurts scored 0.6 points, Samuel 4.2, the 49ers D/ST 6 and Evan McPherson 8, while Williams, Njoku and Kupp each recorded zero. The final score was Habibsters 251.36, Team Pillbert 192.08.

Amon-Ra St. Brown was the standout of the final for Habibsters, scoring 43 points against a projection of 29.7, well above his regular-season rate of 14.3 points per start for the team. The quarterback pair of Dak Prescott (45.5 points, projected 43.2) and Josh Allen (44.2, projected 39.9) both beat expectations; Allen had averaged 23.2 points across 15 earlier starts. Evan Engram added 27.9 points against a 19.2 projection, comfortably above his 9.2-point season average, and the two defenses outscored their projections by a combined 20.9 points, with the Bills D/ST at 19 (projected 8) and the Jets D/ST at 18 (projected 8.1).

Habibsters won in spite of its running backs. Christian McCaffrey, the semifinal hero, scored 11.1 points against a 23.2 projection, all of it in week 17, after averaging 21.7 per start during the season. Rachaad White (17.9 against 30), Austin Ekeler (11.9 against 26.6) and Tony Pollard (21 against 26.2) also fell short. Najee Harris scored 46 points on the Habibsters bench, more than any starter in the game, though the margin made the oversight a historical footnote rather than a costly one.

For Team Pillbert, Joe Mixon was the top performer with 40.9 points against a 29.3 projection, far above his 12.8-point season average. Kyren Williams scored 29.1, all in week 17. The decisive shortfall came at quarterback: Jalen Hurts, projected for 44.2 points, finished with 19.8, and Tyreek Hill managed 28.3 against a 37.7 projection after averaging 19.2 per start in the regular season.

Philly's bench held C.J. Stroud at 33.5 points, including 20.6 in week 18, compared with Hurts' 0.6 that week. Sam LaPorta (23.3), Isiah Pacheco (26) and Kenneth Walker III (23.6) also scored on the bench. Even with the best available week 18 substitutions, however, Team Pillbert could not have recovered roughly 45 points, short of the 59.3-point margin, so no lineup change would have altered the result.

The victory made Kaushal the first champion in Buckaroo Football League history and Habibsters the first name on the trophy. The 59.3-point margin also ensured that the inaugural final, forecast by Luffy as a near coin flip, ended as a decisive win. Team Pillbert finished second of six, and Alan's 19.8-point lead after week 17 stands as the first lead to slip away in a Buckaroo Bowl.

Habib went on to win Buckaroo Bowl II in 2024 as well, making Bowl I the first of back-to-back titles and the foundation of the league's first dynasty. That run ended in 2025, when Sonny won Buckaroo Bowl III with Ben Dover. The bottom of the 2023 standings belonged to Sonny as well: Ben Dover finished last via the consolation ladder, the first of two straight last-place finishes before his eventual title.
